property_summary: For any caller equal to the current owner, calling setOwner(newOwner) always makes c.owner() equal newOwner; the mutant deletes the assignment so the owner never changes and the rule fails for any newOwner different from the old one.
For any caller that is not the current owner, setOwner must revert and leave owner unchanged; the mutant lets that caller overwrite owner.

For any caller and any new owner different from the current one, setOwner succeeds only when the caller is the current owner (owner becomes newOwner) and otherwise reverts leaving owner unchanged; the inverted-require mutant inverts this so an owner's call reverts while a non-owner's call succeeds, breaking the rule.

For any address newOwner, a call to setOwner(newOwner) from the current owner always succeeds and makes owner == newOwner; the mutant rejects the owner's own call, so it reverts for inputs the reference accepts.
For any caller and address, a successful setOwner call returns true; the mutant returns false, breaking this rule.
For any caller equal to the current owner and any new owner address, setOwner must complete and return true; the mutant returns false for the same calls.

property_summary: For any new owner address, a call from the current owner succeeds without reverting and returns true while transferring ownership; the mutant instead returns false on such successful calls.

For any caller equal to the current owner and any new address, a successful setOwner call must set the owner to that address and return exactly true; the mutant never changes the owner and returns owner != _owner, which is false when _owner equals the current owner (or when the new owner equals the old one).

For any caller equal to the current owner and any proposed address (including the current owner itself), a successful setOwner call must return exactly true; the mutant returns (owner != _owner), which is false whenever _owner equals the current owner.

For any caller who is the owner and any fuzzed address, a successful setOwner must make c.owner() equal that address; the mutant never updates the owner, so c.owner() stays the deployer whenever a different address is fuzzed.

For any caller who is the current owner and any admissible address x, a successful call setOwner(x) must leave c.owner() equal to x; the mutant instead stores msg.sender, so it breaks whenever x differs from the owner.

property_summary: For any caller that is not the current owner, setOwner must revert and leave the owner unchanged; the mutant lets any caller change it, so some non-owner caller succeeds and c.owner() differs from P's.
After any successful setOwner(newOwner) by the current owner, c.owner() must equal newOwner; the mutant instead sets owner to the caller, so for any caller distinct from newOwner the assertion fails.
For any caller who is the owner, a successful setOwner call must return true; the mutant deletes the named return so it returns false.
m_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address): successful owner setOwner must return true and update owner

property_summary: For any address newOwner, calling setOwner(newOwner) as the current owner sets c.owner() to exactly newOwner; the mutant instead sets it to msg.sender, so any newOwner != msg.sender breaks the rule.

For any admissible newOwner, a call to setOwner made by the current owner always sets c.owner() to exactly that newOwner; the mutant instead sets it to msg.sender, so any newOwner different from the caller breaks the rule.

For every candidate address, calling setOwner as the current owner must set c.owner() to exactly that address; the buggy version instead sets owner to the zero address, breaking this for any nonzero candidate.

For any nonzero account that becomes the owner, a later setOwner by that account to any address stores exactly that address; the mutant instead stores the zero address, so c.owner() no longer equals the requested value.

For any admissible new owner address (nonzero), calling setOwner as the current owner sets owner to exactly that address; the mutant instead always sets it to address(0), which differs whenever the supplied address is nonzero.
For any caller that is not the current owner, setOwner must revert and leave owner unchanged; the mutant's always-true modifier lets such a caller overwrite owner, so owner differs.

For any caller authorized as owner and any candidate address, a successful setOwner call must return true and actually transfer ownership to that address; the mutant's early return makes every such call return false without changing the owner.

For any caller equal to the current owner and any address newOwner, a successful setOwner(newOwner) leaves c.owner() equal to newOwner; the mutant overwrites it to address(0), breaking this for any newOwner != address(0).

For any caller who is the current owner and any non-zero newOwner, a successful setOwner(newOwner) must leave c.owner() equal to newOwner; the mutant overwrites it to address(0), violating this for every non-zero newOwner.
